title.zh: 卷77 列傳第42 隱逸
title.raw: 卷77 列傳第42 隱逸 Volume 77 Biographies 42: Recluses

sentences.zh: 隋書卷七十七列傳第四十二

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 77, Biography 42
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 77, Biography 42

sentences.zh: ○隱逸

translations.literal: ○ Recluses
translations.idiomatic: ○ Recluses

sentences.zh: 自肇有書契，綿曆百王，雖時有盛衰，未嘗無隱逸之士。

translations.literal: From the beginning when there were writing and tallies, spanning the hundred kings, although times had rise and decline, there had never been lacking reclusive scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since writing and records began and dynasties succeeded one another through the ages, times might wax and wane, yet men who lived in reclusion had never been absent.

sentences.zh: 故《易》稱「遁世無悶」，又曰「不事王侯」；

translations.literal: Therefore the Changes says "withdrawn from the world without distress," and also says "does not serve kings and marquises";
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Changes speaks of one who "withdraws from the world without vexation," and also of one who "does not serve kings and lords";

sentences.zh: 《詩》雲「皎皎白駒，在彼空谷」；

translations.literal: The Odes says "Bright, bright is the white colt, in that empty valley";
translations.idiomatic: the Book of Odes says, "Gleaming bright is the white colt in the hollow vale";

sentences.zh: 《禮》雲「儒有上不臣天子，下不事王侯」；

translations.literal: The Rites says "the Ru scholar above does not take the Son of Heaven as lord, below does not serve kings and marquises";
translations.idiomatic: the Book of Rites says, "The scholar, on high, does not treat the Son of Heaven as his lord; below, he does not serve kings and lords";

sentences.zh: 語曰「舉逸民，天下之人歸心焉」。

translations.literal: A saying goes "raise up retired people, and the people of the empire will turn their hearts to you."
translations.idiomatic: and the Analects says, "Raise up those in retirement, and all under Heaven will turn their hearts to you."

sentences.zh: 雖出處殊途，語默異用，各言其志，皆君子之道也。

translations.literal: Although in going out and staying in they took different roads, in speech and silence they had different usages, each expressed his aim—all were the way of the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Though their paths of action and withdrawal differed and their modes of speech and silence diverged, each pursued his own purpose—these were all ways of the true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 洪崖兆其始，箕山扇其風，七人作乎周年，四皓光乎漢日，魏、晉以降，其流逾廣。

translations.literal: Hongya signaled the beginning, Jishan fanned the wind, the Seven Men arose in the Zhou cycle, the Four Hoary Heads shone in Han days—from Wei and Jin onward, their stream grew ever broader.
translations.idiomatic: Hongya marked the beginning, Jishan gave the custom its breeze; the Seven Worthies appeared in the Zhou age, the Four White Heads shone in Han times—and from Wei and Jin onward their current spread ever wider.

sentences.zh: 其大者則輕天下，細萬物，其小者則安苦節，甘賤貧。

translations.literal: The greater among them slighted All-under-Heaven and regarded all things as minute; the lesser were content with hardship and integrity, finding poverty sweet.
translations.idiomatic: The great among them held the realm lightly and treated the myriad things as trifles; the lesser were content with stern integrity and took poverty as their joy.

sentences.zh: 或與世同塵，隨波瀾以俱逝，或違時矯俗，望江湖而獨往。

translations.literal: Some shared the world's dust and drifted away with the waves; some defied the times and corrected custom, gazing toward rivers and lakes as they went alone.
translations.idiomatic: Some mingled with the world and were carried off with its currents; others defied their age and set themselves apart from convention, turning their gaze to rivers and lakes as they went their own way.

sentences.zh: 狎玩魚鳥，左右琴書，拾遺粒而織落毛，飲石泉而廕松柏。

translations.literal: They played with fish and birds, kept zither and books at hand, gathered fallen grains and wove shed feathers, drank from stone springs and sheltered beneath pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: They delighted in fish and birds, kept zither and books close at hand, gathered stray grains and wove shed feathers, drank from stony springs and rested in the shade of pines and cypresses.

sentences.zh: 放情宇宙之外，自足懷抱之中，然皆欣欣於獨善，鮮汲汲於兼濟。

translations.literal: They released their feelings beyond the cosmos and found sufficiency within their own bosoms; yet all rejoiced in cultivating themselves alone, rarely pressing urgently to benefit all together.
translations.idiomatic: They let their hearts roam beyond the universe and found contentment within their own breasts; yet all rejoiced in perfecting themselves alone, and few were eager to bring benefit to the world at large.

sentences.zh: 而受命哲王，守文令主，莫不束帛交馳，蒲輪結轍，奔走岩穀，唯恐不逮者，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet sage kings who received the Mandate and cultured rulers who preserved the tradition—none failed to send silken cords crisscrossing and rush-wheeled carts wheel-rutted, rushing to mountain valleys for fear of not reaching them—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet sage kings who received the Mandate and cultured rulers who upheld the tradition—none failed to send silken cords back and forth and rush-wheeled carriages in long processions, hurrying to mountain valleys for fear of not reaching them in time—why was this?

sentences.zh: 以其道雖未弘，志不可奪，縱無舟楫之功，終有賢貞之操。

translations.literal: Because although their Way was not yet broadly spread, their resolve could not be wrested away; even if they lacked the achievement of boat and oar, in the end they had the integrity of worthiness and constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Because although their Way had not been broadly realized, their resolve could not be broken; even without the achievement of steering the state, they still possessed the integrity of worthiness and constancy.

sentences.zh: 足以立懦夫之志，息貪競之風，與夫苟得之徒，不可同年共日。

translations.literal: They were sufficient to establish the resolve of cowards and quell the wind of greedy competition; with those who grasp gain by any means, they could not be mentioned in the same year or day.
translations.idiomatic: They were enough to stiffen the resolve of the timid and still the wind of greedy rivalry; they could not be spoken of in the same breath as those who seize profit by any means.

sentences.zh: 所謂無用以為用，無為而無不為者也。

translations.literal: This is what is called using the useless as use, acting without acting yet leaving nothing undone.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by using the useless as use, and by acting without acting yet leaving nothing undone.

sentences.zh: 故敘其人，列其行，以備《隱逸篇》云。

translations.literal: Therefore I narrate these persons and array their conduct, to complete the "Recluses" section.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I relate their lives and set forth their conduct, to complete this chapter on recluses.

sentences.zh: ○李士謙

translations.literal: ○ Li Shiqian
translations.idiomatic: ○ Li Shiqian

sentences.zh: 李士謙，字子約，趙郡平棘人也。

translations.literal: Li Shiqian, style Ziyue, was a native of Pingji in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiqian, styled Ziyue, was a native of Pingji in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 髫齔喪父，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: In infancy he lost his father and became known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father in childhood and became known for his filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 母曾嘔吐，疑為中毒，因跪而嘗之。

translations.literal: His mother once vomited; suspecting poison, he knelt and tasted it.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother once vomited, fearing she had been poisoned, he knelt and tasted the vomit himself.

sentences.zh: 伯父魏岐州刺史瑒，深所嗟尚，每稱曰：「此兒吾家之顏子也。」

translations.literal: His uncle Yang, Inspector of Qizhou in Wei, deeply admired him and would often say, "This boy is the Yan Hui of our family."
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yang, who served as Inspector of Qizhou in Wei, held him in deep admiration and would often say, "This boy is the Yan Hui of our house."

sentences.zh: 年十二，魏廣平王贊辟開府參軍事。

translations.literal: At age twelve, Zan, Prince of Guangping of Wei, recruited him as Record Keeper of the Prince's Household Staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of twelve, Zan, Prince of Guangping of Wei, recruited him as Record Keeper of the Prince's Household Staff.

sentences.zh: 後丁母憂，居喪骨立。

translations.literal: Later, upon his mother's death, in mourning he was reduced to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his mother died, he mourned until he was skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 有姊適宋氏，不勝哀而死。

translations.literal: He had an elder sister married to the Song clan who, unable to bear the grief, died.
translations.idiomatic: An elder sister of his, married into the Song clan, died of grief she could not bear.

sentences.zh: 士謙服闋，舍宅為伽藍，脫身而出。

translations.literal: When Shiqian's mourning period ended, he gave his house to become a monastery and withdrew from worldly life.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiqian's mourning period ended, he gave his house over to become a Buddhist monastery and withdrew from worldly life.

sentences.zh: 詣學請業，研精不倦，遂博覽群籍，兼善天文術數。

translations.literal: He went to school to seek learning, studying with tireless refinement, and came to read broadly in all books, also excelling in astronomy and numerology.
translations.idiomatic: He went to study and pursued learning with tireless refinement, eventually reading widely in all the classics and also excelling in astronomy and numerology.

sentences.zh: 齊吏部尚書辛術召署員外郎，趙郡王睿舉德行，皆稱疾不就。

translations.literal: Xin Shu, Minister of the Civil Service in Qi, summoned him to serve as Supernumerary Gentleman; Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery recommended him for moral conduct—on each occasion he pleaded illness and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Shu, Minister of the Civil Service in Qi, summoned him to serve as Supernumerary Gentleman, and Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery recommended him for moral conduct—each time he pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 和士開亦重其名，將諷朝廷，擢為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He Shikai also valued his reputation and was about to prompt the court to promote him to Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai also valued his reputation and intended to prompt the court to appoint him Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 士謙知而固辭，得免。

translations.literal: Shiqian learned of it and firmly declined, and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian learned of this and firmly declined, and so was spared the appointment.

sentences.zh: 隋有天下，畢志不仕。

translations.literal: When Sui possessed the empire, he fulfilled his resolve and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui came to rule the empire, he held firm to his resolve and never took office.

sentences.zh: 自以少孤，未嘗飲酒食肉，口無殺害之言。

translations.literal: Because he had been orphaned young, he never drank wine or ate meat, and his mouth held no words of killing.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had been orphaned young, he never drank wine or ate meat, and never spoke words of killing.

sentences.zh: 至於親賓來萃，輒陳樽俎，對之危坐，終日不倦。

translations.literal: When relatives and guests gathered, he would set out wine and meat, sit upright facing them, and remain tireless all day.
translations.idiomatic: When relatives and guests gathered, he would set out wine and meat for them, sit upright in their company, and keep at it all day without tiring.

sentences.zh: 李氏宗党豪盛，每至春秋二社，必高會極歡，無不沉醉喧亂。

translations.literal: The Li clan's lineage and kin were powerful and flourishing; whenever the spring and autumn communal sacrifices came, they would hold grand gatherings of utmost revelry, none failing to become drunk and riotous.
translations.idiomatic: The Li clan was powerful and numerous; whenever the spring and autumn communal sacrifices arrived, they held grand gatherings of utmost revelry, and none failed to end up drunk and disorderly.

sentences.zh: 嘗集士謙所，盛饌盈前，而先為設黍，謂群從曰：「孔子稱黍為五穀之長，荀卿亦雲食先黍稷，古人所尚，容可違乎？」

translations.literal: They once gathered at Shiqian's place with lavish fare spread before them, yet he first set out millet and said to the assembled kin, "Confucius called millet the chief of the five grains; Xun Qing also said that in eating one should put millet and glutinous millet first—what the ancients honored—how could one go against this?"
translations.idiomatic: They once gathered at Shiqian's home with lavish fare spread before them, yet he first set out millet and said to the assembled kin, "Confucius called millet the chief of the five grains, and Xunzi also said that in eating one should put millet and glutinous millet first—what the ancients honored—how could one go against this?"

sentences.zh: 少長肅然，不敢馳惰，退而相謂曰：「既見君子，方覺吾徒之不德也。」

translations.literal: Young and old became solemn, not daring to be lax or idle; afterward they said to one another, "Having seen a gentleman, we now realize how lacking in virtue we ourselves are."
translations.idiomatic: Young and old grew solemn and dared not be lax; afterward they said to one another, "Having seen a gentleman, we now realize how lacking in virtue we ourselves are."

sentences.zh: 士謙聞而自責曰：「何乃為人所疏，頓至於此！」

translations.literal: Shiqian heard and blamed himself, saying, "How have I come to be held aloof by others, to this sudden degree!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shiqian heard this, he blamed himself, saying, "How have I come to be held at a distance by others, to this sudden degree!"

sentences.zh: 家富於財，躬處節儉，每以振施為務。

translations.literal: His household was rich in wealth, yet he personally practiced thrift and made relief and giving his constant task.
translations.idiomatic: His household was wealthy, yet he personally practiced thrift and made relief and charity his constant concern.

sentences.zh: 州裡有喪事不辦者，士謙輒奔走赴之，隨乏供濟。

translations.literal: When someone in the district could not manage a funeral, Shiqian would hurry to help and supply whatever was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: When someone in the district could not manage a funeral, Shiqian would hurry to assist and supply whatever was lacking.

sentences.zh: 有兄弟分財不均，至相鬩訟，士謙聞而出財，補其少者，令與多者相埒。

translations.literal: When brothers divided property unequally and came to quarrel and sue, Shiqian heard of it, contributed funds, supplemented the one who had less, and made him equal to the one who had more.
translations.idiomatic: When brothers divided property unequally and came to quarrel and sue one another, Shiqian heard of it, contributed funds to supplement the one who had less, and made his share equal to his brother's.

sentences.zh: 兄弟愧懼，更相推讓，卒為善士。

translations.literal: The brothers, ashamed and afraid, yielded to one another in turn and in the end became good men.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers, ashamed and afraid, yielded to one another in turn and in the end became good men.

sentences.zh: 有牛犯其田者，士謙牽置涼處飼之，過於本主。

translations.literal: When an ox trespassed on his fields, Shiqian led it to a cool place and fed it, treating it better than its own owner.
translations.idiomatic: When an ox trespassed on his fields, Shiqian led it to a cool place and fed it, treating it better than its own owner did.

sentences.zh: 望見盜刈其禾黍者，默而避之。

translations.literal: When he saw thieves reaping his grain and millet, he kept silent and withdrew from them.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw thieves reaping his grain and millet, he kept silent and withdrew from them.

sentences.zh: 其家僮嘗執盜粟者，士謙慰諭之曰：「窮困所致，義無相責。」

translations.literal: His household slave once seized a thief of grain; Shiqian comforted and instructed him, saying, "Poverty drove him to it—by right one should not blame him."
translations.idiomatic: When a household slave once seized a thief of grain, Shiqian comforted him and said, "Poverty drove him to it—by right one should not blame him."

sentences.zh: 遽令放之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered him released.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered the man released.

sentences.zh: 其奴嘗與鄉人董震因醉角力，震扼其喉，斃於手下。

translations.literal: His slave once wrestled with a fellow townsman named Dong Zhen while drunk; Zhen seized his throat and killed him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: His slave once wrestled while drunk with a fellow townsman named Dong Zhen; Zhen seized his throat and killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 震惶懼請罪，士謙謂之曰：「卿本無殺心，何為相謝！

translations.literal: Zhen, fearful and afraid, begged forgiveness; Shiqian said to him, "You originally had no intent to kill—why apologize!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, fearful and remorseful, begged forgiveness; Shiqian said to him, "You had no intent to kill—why apologize!

sentences.zh: 然可遠去，無為吏之所拘。」

translations.literal: Yet you should go far away, lest the officials seize you."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you should go far away, lest the officials seize you."

sentences.zh: 性寬厚，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His nature was generous and mild—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was generous and mild—all his conduct was of this kind.

sentences.zh: 其後出粟數千石，以貸鄉人，值年穀不登，債家無以償，皆來致謝。

translations.literal: Later he distributed several thousand bushels of grain to lend to his fellow townspeople; when the year's harvest failed, the debtor households had no means to repay and all came to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Later he distributed several thousand bushels of grain to lend to his fellow townspeople; when the year's harvest failed, the debtor households had no means to repay and all came to apologize.

sentences.zh: 士謙曰：「吾家餘粟，本圖振贍，豈求利哉！」

translations.literal: Shiqian said, "The surplus grain in my household was originally intended for relief and support—how could I seek profit!"
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian said, "The surplus grain in my household was meant for relief and support—how could I seek profit from it!"

sentences.zh: 於是悉召債家，為設酒食，對之燔契，曰：「債了矣，幸勿為念也。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned all the debtor households, set out wine and food for them, and burned the contracts before them, saying, "The debt is settled—please do not brood on it."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he summoned all the debtor households, set out wine and food, and burned the contracts before them, saying, "The debt is settled—please do not brood on it."

sentences.zh: 各令罷去。

translations.literal: He had each of them depart.
translations.idiomatic: He had each of them depart.

sentences.zh: 明年大熟，債家爭來償謙，謙拒之，一無所受。

translations.literal: The next year the harvest was abundant; the debtor households vied to repay Shiqian, but he refused them and accepted nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the harvest was abundant; the debtor households vied to repay Shiqian, but he refused them and accepted nothing.

sentences.zh: 他年又大饑，多有死者，士謙罄竭家資，為之糜粥，賴以全活者將萬計。

translations.literal: Another year there was again great famine and many died; Shiqian exhausted his household's resources to make gruel for them, and those who lived through it by his aid numbered nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Another year brought great famine and many deaths; Shiqian exhausted his household's resources to make gruel for the hungry, and those who survived by his aid numbered nearly ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 收埋骸骨，所見無遺。

translations.literal: He gathered and buried the bones of the dead—none he saw were left unattended.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered and buried the bones of the dead—none that he saw were left unattended.

sentences.zh: 至春，又出糧種，分給貧乏。

translations.literal: When spring came, he again distributed grain and seed to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: When spring came, he again distributed grain and seed to the poor.

sentences.zh: 趙郡農民德之，撫其子孫曰：「此乃李參軍遺惠也。」

translations.literal: The farmers of Zhao Commandery were grateful to him and would stroke their sons and grandsons, saying, "This is the lingering kindness left by Registrar Li."
translations.idiomatic: The farmers of Zhao Commandery were grateful to him and would tell their sons and grandsons, "This is the lingering kindness left by Registrar Li."

sentences.zh: 或謂士謙曰：「子多陰德。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Shiqian, "Sir, you have much hidden virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Shiqian, "Sir, you have much hidden virtue."

sentences.zh: 士謙曰：「所謂陰德者何？

translations.literal: Shiqian said, "What is meant by hidden virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian said, "What is meant by hidden virtue?

sentences.zh: 猶耳鳴，已獨聞之，人無知者。

translations.literal: It is like ringing in the ears—one alone hears it, and others know nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: It is like ringing in the ears—one alone hears it, and others know nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 今吾所作，吾子皆知，何陰德之有！」

translations.literal: What I do now, my sons all know—how could there be hidden virtue!"
translations.idiomatic: What I do now, my sons all know—how could there be hidden virtue!"

sentences.zh: 士謙善談玄理，嘗有一客在坐，不信佛家應報之義，以為外典無聞焉。

translations.literal: Shiqian was skilled at discussing arcane principles; once a guest was seated who did not believe in the Buddhist doctrine of retribution, thinking that the external classics had no mention of it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian was skilled at discussing arcane principles; once when a guest was present who did not believe in the Buddhist doctrine of karmic retribution, thinking that the secular classics made no mention of it.

sentences.zh: 士謙喻之曰：「積善余慶，積惡余殃，高門待封，掃墓望喪，豈非休咎之應邪？

translations.literal: Shiqian instructed him, saying, "Accumulate goodness and blessings remain; accumulate evil and calamities remain—great gates await enfeoffment, sweeping tombs await mourning—are these not responses of fortune and misfortune?
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian explained to him, "Accumulate goodness and blessings remain; accumulate evil and calamities remain—great houses await enfeoffment, sweeping tombs await mourning—are these not responses of fortune and misfortune?

sentences.zh: 佛經雲輪轉五道，無複窮已，此則賈誼所言，千變萬化，未始有極，忽然為人之謂也。

translations.literal: The Buddhist sutras say that revolving through the five paths has no end—this is what Jia Yi spoke of: a thousand transformations and ten thousand changes, never having a limit, suddenly becoming human.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist sutras say that revolving through the five paths of existence has no end—this is what Jia Yi meant when he spoke of a thousand transformations and ten thousand changes without limit, of suddenly becoming human.

sentences.zh: 佛道未東，而賢者已知其然矣。

translations.literal: Before the Buddhist Way came east, worthy men already knew that it was so.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Buddhist Way came east, worthy men already knew that it was so.

sentences.zh: 至若鯀為黃熊，杜宇為鶗鴂，褒君為龍，牛哀為獸，君子為鵠，小人為猿，彭生為豕，如意為犬，黃母為黿，宣武為鱉，鄧艾為牛，徐伯為魚，鈴下為烏，書生為蛇，羊祜前身，李氏之子，此非佛家變受異形之謂邪？」

translations.literal: As for Gun becoming a yellow bear, Du Yu becoming a cuckoo, Lord Bao becoming a dragon, Niu Ai becoming a beast, the gentleman becoming a swan, the petty man becoming an ape, Peng Sheng becoming a pig, Ruyi becoming a dog, Lady Huang becoming a soft-shelled turtle, Xuan Wu becoming a river turtle, Deng Ai becoming an ox, Xu Bo becoming a fish, the bell-ringer becoming a crow, the scholar becoming a snake, Yang Hu's former body, the son of the Li clan—is this not what the Buddhist school calls transformation and receiving of different forms?"
translations.idiomatic: Consider Gun becoming a yellow bear, Du Yu becoming a cuckoo, Lord Bao becoming a dragon, Niu Ai becoming a beast, the gentleman becoming a swan, the petty man becoming an ape, Peng Sheng becoming a pig, Ruyi becoming a dog, Lady Huang becoming a soft-shelled turtle, Xuan Wu becoming a river turtle, Deng Ai becoming an ox, Xu Bo becoming a fish, the bell-ringer becoming a crow, the scholar becoming a snake, Yang Hu's former incarnation, the son of the Li clan—are these not what Buddhism calls transformation into different forms?"

sentences.zh: 客曰：「邢子才雲，豈有松柏後身化為樗櫟，僕以為然。」

translations.literal: The guest said, "Xing Zicai said, how could a pine or cypress in a later body transform into a foul tree—I think he was right."
translations.idiomatic: The guest said, "Xing Zicai said that a pine or cypress could not in a later life transform into a foul tree—I think he was right."

sentences.zh: 士謙曰：「此不類之談也。

translations.literal: Shiqian said, "This is talk that does not belong to the same category.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian said, "That is talk that misses the point.

sentences.zh: 變化皆由心而作，木豈有心乎？」

translations.literal: Transformations all proceed from the mind—how could wood have a mind?"
translations.idiomatic: Transformations all proceed from the mind—how could wood have a mind?"

sentences.zh: 客又問三教優劣，士謙曰：「佛，日也；

translations.literal: The guest again asked about the relative merits of the three teachings; Shiqian said, "Buddhism is the sun;
translations.idiomatic: The guest again asked about the relative merits of the three teachings; Shiqian said, "Buddhism is the sun;

sentences.zh: 道，月也，儒，五星也。」

translations.literal: the Way is the moon; Confucianism is the five stars."
translations.idiomatic: the Way is the moon; Confucianism is the five stars."

sentences.zh: 客亦不能難而止。

translations.literal: The guest also could not refute him and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The guest could not refute him and let the matter rest.

sentences.zh: 士謙平生喜為詠懷詩，輒毀棄其本，不以示人。

translations.literal: Shiqian throughout his life delighted in composing lyric poems of reflection, but would always destroy the drafts and not show them to others.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life Shiqian delighted in composing lyric poems of reflection, but would always destroy the drafts and never show them to others.

sentences.zh: 又嘗論刑罰，遺文不具，其略曰：「帝王制法，沿革不同，自可損益，無為頓改。

translations.literal: He also once discussed punishments; the transmitted text is incomplete. The gist says, "Emperors and kings make laws; following and changing differ—one may naturally increase or decrease them, but need not change them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: He also once discussed punishments; the transmitted text is incomplete. The gist runs, "Emperors and kings make laws; each age follows and changes them differently—one may naturally increase or decrease them, but need not change them all at once.

sentences.zh: 今之贓重者死，是酷而不懲也。

translations.literal: Today the corrupt who take heavily are put to death—this is cruel yet does not restrain.
translations.idiomatic: Today the corrupt who take heavily are put to death—this is cruel yet does not restrain.

sentences.zh: 語曰：'人不畏死，不可以死恐之。

translations.literal: A saying goes, 'When people do not fear death, one cannot frighten them with death.'
translations.idiomatic: A saying goes, 'When people do not fear death, one cannot frighten them with death.'

sentences.zh: '愚謂此罪宜從肉刑，刖其一趾，再犯者斷其右腕。

translations.literal: I foolishly think that for this crime one should apply corporal punishment: amputate one toe; for a second offense, sever the right wrist.
translations.idiomatic: I think that for this crime one should apply corporal punishment: amputate one toe; for a second offense, sever the right wrist.

sentences.zh: 流刑刖去右手三指，又犯者下其腕。

translations.literal: For exile punishment, amputate three fingers of the right hand; for another offense, remove the wrist.
translations.idiomatic: For exile punishment, amputate three fingers of the right hand; for another offense, remove the wrist.

sentences.zh: 小盜宜黥，又犯則落其所用三指，又不悛下其腕，無不止也。

translations.literal: Petty thieves should be tattooed; for another offense, remove the three fingers they use; if still unrepentant, remove the wrist—none would fail to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Petty thieves should be tattooed; for another offense, remove the three fingers they use; if still unrepentant, remove the wrist—none would fail to stop.

sentences.zh: 無賴之人，竄之邊裔，職為亂階，適所以召戎矣，非求治之道也。

translations.literal: Ruffians, when banished to the borderlands, in their posts become steps to disorder—this is precisely what summons the barbarians; it is not the way to seek good government.
translations.idiomatic: When ruffians are banished to the borderlands, they become agents of disorder—this is precisely what summons the barbarians; it is not the way to seek good government.

sentences.zh: 博弈淫遊，盜之萌也，禁而不止，黥之則可。」

translations.literal: Gambling and licentious roaming are the sprouts of theft; if prohibition does not stop it, tattooing will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Gambling and licentious roaming are the sprouts of theft; if prohibition does not stop it, tattooing will suffice."

sentences.zh: 有識者頗以為得治體。

translations.literal: Men of insight largely thought he had grasped the substance of good government.
translations.idiomatic: Men of insight largely thought he had grasped the substance of good government.

sentences.zh: 開皇八年，終於家，時年六十六。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaihuang, he died at home, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaihuang, he died at home, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 趙郡士女聞之，莫不流涕曰：「我曹不死，而令李參軍死乎！」

translations.literal: When the men and women of Zhao Commandery heard it, none failed to weep and say, "We do not die, yet Registrar Li is made to die!"
translations.idiomatic: When the men and women of Zhao Commandery heard of it, none failed to weep and say, "We do not die, yet Registrar Li is made to die!"

sentences.zh: 會葬者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Those who attended the funeral numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand people attended his funeral.

sentences.zh: 鄉人李景伯等以士謙道著丘園，條其行狀，詣尚書省請先生之諡，事寢不行，遂相與樹碑於墓。

translations.literal: Fellow townsman Li Jingbo and others, because Shiqian's Way was manifest in field and garden, set forth his conduct in detail and went to the Ministry of Personnel to request a posthumous title for the gentleman; the matter was shelved and did not proceed, so they together erected a stele at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsman Li Jingbo and others, because Shiqian's Way was manifest in field and garden, set forth his conduct in detail and went to the Ministry of Personnel to request a posthumous title for him; the matter was shelved and did not proceed, so they together erected a stele at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 其妻范陽盧氏，亦有婦德，及夫終後，所有賻贈，一無所受，謂州裡父老曰：「參軍平生好施，今雖殞歿，安可奪其志哉！」

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Lu of Fanyang, also had the virtue of a wife; when her husband ended, all funeral gifts she received not one, and said to the district elders, "The Registrar all his life delighted in giving; now though he has perished, how can one wrest away his resolve!"
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Lu of Fanyang, also possessed wifely virtue; when her husband died, she accepted none of the funeral gifts offered and said to the district elders, "The Registrar all his life delighted in giving; now that he has died, how can one wrest away his resolve!"

sentences.zh: 於是散粟五百石以賑窮乏。

translations.literal: Thereupon she distributed five hundred bushels of grain to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon she distributed five hundred bushels of grain to relieve the poor.

sentences.zh: 崔廓子賾

translations.literal: Cui Kuo's son Ze
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuo's son Ze

sentences.zh: 崔廓，字士玄，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Cui Kuo, style Shixuan, was a native of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuo, styled Shixuan, was a native of Anping in Boling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父子元，齊燕州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Ziyuan was Administrator of Yanzhou in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ziyuan served as Administrator of Yanzhou in Qi.

sentences.zh: 廓少孤貧而母賤，由是不為邦族所齒。

translations.literal: Kuo was orphaned young and poor, and his mother was of low status; for this reason he was not ranked among the clan and kin of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was orphaned young and poor, and his mother was of low status; for this reason the clan and local community did not regard him as their equal.

sentences.zh: 初為裡佐，屢逢屈辱，於是感激，逃入山中。

translations.literal: At first he served as village aide and repeatedly met with humiliation; stirred by this, he fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as village aide and repeatedly met with humiliation; stirred by this, he fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 遂博覽書籍，多所通涉，山東學者皆宗之。

translations.literal: He then read broadly in books and penetrated many fields; scholars east of the mountains all took him as their master.
translations.idiomatic: He then read broadly in books and mastered many fields; scholars east of the mountains all took him as their master.

sentences.zh: 既還鄉里，不應辟命。

translations.literal: When he returned to his native place, he did not respond to summons.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to his native place, he did not respond to official summons.

sentences.zh: 與郡李士謙為忘言之友，每相往來，時稱崔、李。

translations.literal: With Li Shiqian of the commandery he was a friend without words, visiting each other constantly; their day they were called Cui and Li.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Shiqian of the commandery he was a friend who needed no words, visiting each other constantly; in their day they were called Cui and Li.

sentences.zh: 及士謙死，廓哭之慟，為之作傳，輸之秘府。

translations.literal: When Shiqian died, Kuo mourned him bitterly, composed a biography for him, and submitted it to the Imperial Archives.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiqian died, Kuo mourned him bitterly, composed a biography for him, and submitted it to the Imperial Archives.

sentences.zh: 士謙妻盧氏寡居，每有家事，輒令人諮廓取定。

translations.literal: Shiqian's wife, Lady Lu, lived as a widow; whenever there was a household matter, she would have someone consult Kuo for a decision.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian's widow, Lady Lu, whenever there was a household matter would have someone consult Kuo for a decision.

sentences.zh: 郭嘗著論，言刑名之理，其義甚精，文多不載。

translations.literal: Kuo once wrote a treatise, speaking of the principles of punishment and names; its meaning was very refined, but most of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo once wrote a treatise on the principles of law and nomenclature; though its argument was exceedingly fine, most of the work was never preserved.

sentences.zh: 大業中，終於家，時年八十。

translations.literal: During the Daye era, he died at home, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye period he died at home, at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 有子曰賾。

translations.literal: He had a son named Ze.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Ze.

sentences.zh: 賾字祖浚，七歲能屬文，容貌短小，有口才。

translations.literal: Ze, style Zujun, at seven years could compose literary pieces; his appearance was short in stature, and he had eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Ze, styled Zujun, could compose essays at seven; he was short in stature but gifted with a ready tongue.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，秦孝王薦之，射策高第，詔與諸儒定禮樂，授校書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Prince of Qin Xia recommended him; in the archery-and-policy examination he ranked at the top; an edict appointed him with various Confucians to fix rites and music, and he was made Collator.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang reign, Prince Xiao of Qin recommended him; he placed at the top of the policy examination and was ordered to join the Confucian scholars in fixing rites and music, receiving appointment as Collator.

sentences.zh: 尋轉協律郎，太常卿蘇威雅重之。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of Harmonization; Su Wei, Minister of Ceremonies, held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Director of Harmonization, and Su Wei, the Minister of Ceremonies, greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，性至孝，水漿不入口者五日。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he left office; by nature deeply filial, for five days he took no water or broth.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he resigned his post; profoundly filial by nature, he went five days without food or drink.

sentences.zh: 征為河南、豫章二王侍讀，每更日來往二王之第。

translations.literal: Summoned as Reader to the Princes of Henan and Yuzhang, he alternated days traveling between the two princes' residences.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Reader to the Princes of Henan and Yuzhang, spending alternate days at each prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 及河南為晉王，轉記室參軍，自此去豫章。

translations.literal: When Henan became Prince of Jin, he was transferred to Staff Secretary; from then on he left Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Henan was made Prince of Jin, Ze became Staff Secretary and thereafter ceased attending Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 王重之不已，遺賾書曰：

translations.literal: The Prince valued him ever more highly and sent Ze a letter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Prince continued to esteem him and sent Ze a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 昔漢氏西京，梁王建國，平臺、東苑，慕義如林。

translations.literal: In olden days the Han western capital and the Liang prince's founding of his state—with Pingtai and Dongyuan, those who admired righteousness were as thick as a forest.
translations.idiomatic: In the days of the Han western capital and the Liang prince's founding of his realm, at Pingtai and the Eastern Park men who admired virtue gathered like trees in a forest.

sentences.zh: 馬卿辭武騎之官，枚乘罷弘農之守。

translations.literal: Sima Xiangru resigned his post in the Cavalry Guard; Mei Sheng gave up the governorship of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiangru left his post in the Palace Cavalry Guard, and Mei Sheng relinquished the governorship of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 每覽史傳，嘗切怪之，何乃脫略官榮，棲遲籓邸？

translations.literal: Whenever I read the histories, I have deeply wondered: why cast off official glory and linger in a prince's residence?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read the historical records, I have always wondered why they would abandon official honor and settle in a prince's household.

sentences.zh: 以今望古，方知雅志。

translations.literal: Viewing the past from the present, I now understand their lofty intent.
translations.idiomatic: Looking from today back to antiquity, I finally grasp their noble purpose.

sentences.zh: 彼二子者，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: Those two men—surely they were not without purpose!
translations.idiomatic: Those two men surely did not act in vain!

sentences.zh: 足下博聞強記，鉤深致遠，視漢臣之三篋，似涉蒙山，對梁相之五車，若吞雲夢。

translations.literal: You are broadly learned with a strong memory, probing deep and reaching far; compared with the Han minister's three satchels, it is as if crossing Mount Meng; facing the Liang chancellor's five cartloads, it is as if swallowing the Yunmeng marsh.
translations.idiomatic: You are erudite and retentive, probing depths and reaching far; beside the Han minister's three satchels of books you seem to traverse Mount Meng, and before the Liang chancellor's five cartloads you seem to swallow Lake Yunmeng whole.

sentences.zh: 吾兄欽賢重士，敬愛忘疲，先築郭隗之宮，常置穆生之醴。

translations.literal: My elder brother reveres the worthy and esteems scholars, cherishing them without tiring; he first built the palace of Guo Wei and always keeps the wine of Mu Sheng on hand.
translations.idiomatic: My elder brother honors the worthy and cherishes scholars with tireless devotion; he built a palace for Guo Wei and keeps sweet wine ready for Mu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 今者重開土宇，更誓山河，地方七百，牢籠曲阜，城兼七十，包舉臨淄，大啟南陽，方開東閤。

translations.literal: Now he has reopened his domain and renewed his oath over the mountains and rivers; his territory extends seven hundred li, enclosing Qufu; his cities number seventy and more, embracing Linzi; he has greatly opened Nanyang and is now opening the eastern gate.
translations.idiomatic: Now he has reopened his domain and renewed his pledge over land and river; his territory spans seven hundred li, embracing Qufu; his cities exceed seventy, taking in Linzi; he has thrown wide the gates of Nanyang and is now opening his eastern hall to guests.

sentences.zh: 想得奉飛蓋，曳長裾，藉玳筵，躡珠履，歌山桂之偃蹇，賦池竹之檀欒。

translations.literal: I imagine you joining under a flying canopy, trailing a long robe, resting on a tortoiseshell mat, treading in pearl slippers, singing of the towering mountain cassia and composing on the lush pool bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: I picture you riding beneath a flying canopy, trailing your long robe, seated on a tortoiseshell mat in pearl slippers, singing of mountain cassia and composing verses on the bamboo by the pool.

sentences.zh: 其崇貴也如彼，其風流也如此，幸甚幸甚，何樂如之！

translations.literal: His lofty eminence is like that; his refinement is like this—great fortune, great fortune! What joy could compare!
translations.idiomatic: Such is his lofty station, such his elegant bearing—what good fortune, what good fortune! What pleasure could equal it!

sentences.zh: 高視上京，有懷德祖，才謝天人，多慚子建，書不盡意，寧俟繁辭。

translations.literal: Looking down upon the upper capital, I miss Dezao; in talent I fall short of heaven and man; I am much ashamed before Zijian; the letter cannot exhaust my meaning—why await elaborate words?
translations.idiomatic: Gazing toward the capital, I think of Dezao; my talent falls far short of heaven and earth, and I feel deeply ashamed before Zijian; words cannot say all I mean, so why multiply them?

sentences.zh: 賾答曰：

translations.literal: Ze replied:
translations.idiomatic: Ze replied:

sentences.zh: 一昨伏奉教書，榮貺非恆，心靈自失。

translations.literal: The day before yesterday I respectfully received your instructive letter; the honor bestowed was extraordinary, and my spirit was lost within itself.
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday I received your gracious letter; the favor shown me was beyond measure, and my heart was utterly overwhelmed.

sentences.zh: 若乃理高《象》、《系》，管輅思而不解，事富《山海》，郭璞注而未詳。

translations.literal: As for its reasoning, it surpasses the Image and Link texts of the Changes—Guan Lu would ponder without understanding; its content is richer than the Classic of Mountains and Seas—Guo Pu annotated yet could not exhaust it.
translations.idiomatic: Its reasoning rises above the Image and Judgment texts of the Changes—Guan Lu would have pondered in vain; its matter overflows the Classic of Mountains and Seas—even Guo Pu's commentary could not exhaust it.

sentences.zh: 至於五色相宣，八音繁會，鳳鳴不足喻，龍章莫之比。

translations.literal: As for the five colors harmonizing and the eight tones gathering richly—phoenix song is insufficient as analogy; dragon emblems cannot compare.
translations.idiomatic: The five colors blend in harmony and the eight tones assemble in rich concord—phoenix song cannot describe it, and dragon pattern cannot match it.

sentences.zh: 吳劄之論《周頌》，詎盡揄揚，郢客之奏《陽春》，誰堪赴節！

translations.literal: Wu Zha discussing the Zhou Hymns—how could he fully extol it? The guest of Ying playing "Spring in the Capital"—who could match the measure!
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zha discoursed on the Zhou Hymns, he could not fully praise them; when the guest of Ying played "Spring in the Capital," who could keep the beat?

sentences.zh: 伏惟令王殿下，稟潤天潢，承輝日觀，雅道貴于東平，文藝高於北海。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Highness the Illustrious Prince, nourished by the Heavenly River, inheriting radiance from Mount Ri, ranks higher in refined learning than the Prince of Dongping and surpasses the Prince of Beihai in literary art.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness the Illustrious Prince, nourished by the imperial lineage and shining with the sun's radiance, excels the Prince of Dongping in refined conduct and surpasses the Prince of Beihai in literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 漢則馬遷、蕭望，晉則裴楷、張華，雞樹騰聲，鵷池播美，望我清塵，悠然路絕。

translations.literal: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wang; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua—the rooster tree resounds, the egret pool spreads fame; gazing toward my clear dust, the path is serenely cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Han had Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; Jin had Pei Kai and Zhang Hua—your fame resounds like the rooster tree and spreads like the egret pool; looking toward my humble trail, the road between us is impossibly far.

sentences.zh: 祖浚燕南贅客，河朔惰游，本無意于希顏，豈有心于慕藺！

translations.literal: Zujun is a superfluous guest south of the Yan, an idle wanderer north of the River; originally I had no thought of emulating Yan Hui—how could I have a heart set on admiring Lin Xiangru!
translations.idiomatic: Zujun is but an extra guest in the south and a lazy wanderer in the north; I never aspired to emulate Yan Hui—how could I dream of admiring Lin Xiangru!

sentences.zh: 未嘗聚螢映雪，懸頭刺股，讀《論》唯取一篇，披《莊》不過盈尺。

translations.literal: I have never gathered fireflies to read by snow-light, hung my head or pricked my thigh; in reading the Analects I take only one chapter; in opening Zhuangzi I go no more than a full foot's length.
translations.idiomatic: I never studied by firefly or snowlight, never hung from a beam or pricked my thigh; I read only one chapter of the Analects and barely a foot of Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 複況桑榆漸暮，藜藿屢空，舉燭無成，穿楊盡棄。

translations.literal: Moreover, like the mulberry and elm at dusk, I am nearing old age; greens and coarse grains are repeatedly empty; raising the candle brings no achievement; shooting through the willow is all abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, sunset draws near like mulberry and elm at dusk; my larder is often bare; I have achieved nothing by lamplight and abandoned all hope of hitting the willow leaf.

sentences.zh: 但以燕求馬首，薛養雞鳴，謬齒鴻儀，虛班驥皁。

translations.literal: Yet through Yan seeking the horse's head and Xue raising the rooster's crow, I wrongly count myself among the swan's ranks and vainly take place among the thoroughbred blacks.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as Yan sought the horse's head and Xue kept the rooster crowing, I have wrongly taken my place among swans and falsely ranked among thoroughbreds.

sentences.zh: 挾太山而超北海，比報德而非難，堙昆侖以為池，匹酬恩而反易。

translations.literal: To grasp Mount Tai and leap over the North Sea—compared with repaying virtue that is not hard; to dam Mount Kunlun to make a pool—matching return of kindness is instead easy.
translations.idiomatic: Carrying Mount Tai over the North Sea would be easier than repaying your virtue; damming Mount Kunlun to make a pool would be simpler than returning your kindness.

sentences.zh: 忽屬周桐錫瑞，康水承家，門有將相，樹宜桃李。

translations.literal: Suddenly the Zhou paulownia bestows its auspice and the Kang waters inherit the house; at the gate are generals and ministers; the trees are fit for peach and plum.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the Zhou paulownia receives its omen and the house of Kang inherits the realm; generals and ministers stand at your gate, and your trees are fit to bear peach and plum.

sentences.zh: 真龍將下，誰好有名，濫吹先逃，何須別聽！

translations.literal: When the true dragon is about to descend, who will crave fame? The one who blew poorly has already fled—why need anyone else listen!
translations.idiomatic: When the true dragon is about to descend, who still seeks renown? The incompetent musician has already fled—why should anyone else stay to listen!

sentences.zh: 但慈旨抑揚，損上益下，江海所以稱王，丘陵為之不逮。

translations.literal: But your kindly words raise up the lowly and lower the lofty; it is for this that rivers and seas are called kings, and hills and mounds cannot compare.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your gracious words humble yourself and exalt me; rivers and seas are called kings because they lie below, and hills and mounds cannot match them.

sentences.zh: 曹植儻預聞高論，則不隕令名，楊修若切在下風，亦詎虧淳德。

translations.literal: If Cao Zhi had chanced to hear your lofty discourse, he would not lose his fine name; if Yang Xiu were right beneath your wind, he too would not diminish pure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Had Cao Zhi heard your lofty discourse, his fine name would not have fallen; had Yang Xiu stood in your shadow, his pure virtue would not have suffered.

sentences.zh: 無任荷戴之至，謹奉啟以聞。

translations.literal: I cannot bear the utmost of my burdened gratitude; I respectfully submit this letter to inform you.
translations.idiomatic: Overwhelmed with gratitude, I respectfully submit this reply for your notice.

sentences.zh: 豫章得書，賚米五十石，並衣服錢帛。

translations.literal: Yuzhang received the letter and bestowed fifty shi of rice, together with clothing, money, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang received the letter and sent fifty shi of rice along with clothing, money, and silk.

sentences.zh: 時晉邸文翰，多成其手。

translations.literal: At that time the literary compositions of the Prince of Jin's residence were largely written by his hand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time most of the official writings of the Prince of Jin's household came from Ze's pen.

sentences.zh: 王入東宮，除太子齋帥，俄遷舍人。

translations.literal: When the Prince entered the Eastern Palace, Ze was appointed Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Fast; soon he was promoted to Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince entered the Eastern Palace, Ze was made Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Fast and was soon promoted to Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及元德太子薨，以疾歸於家。

translations.literal: When the Yuande Heir Apparent died, Ze returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuande Heir Apparent died, Ze went home, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 後征授起居舍人。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned and appointed Attendant of the Diary of Rest and Movement.
translations.idiomatic: He was later summoned and appointed Attendant of the Imperial Diary.

sentences.zh: 大業四年，從駕汾陽宮，次河陽鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daye, he accompanied the emperor to Fenyang Palace and halted at Heyang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daye he accompanied the emperor to Fenyang Palace and stopped at Heyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 藍田令王曇于藍田山得一玉人，長三尺四寸，著大領衣，冠幘，奏之。

translations.literal: Wang Tan, magistrate of Lantian, obtained a jade figure on Mount Lantian, three feet four inches tall, wearing a broad-collared robe and a headcloth; he reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tan, magistrate of Lantian, found a jade figure on Mount Lantian three feet four inches tall, dressed in a broad-collared robe and wearing a headcloth, and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔問群臣，莫有識者，賾答曰：「謹按漢文已前，未有冠幘，即是文帝以來所製作也。

translations.literal: An edict asked the ministers; none recognized it. Ze replied: "I respectfully note that before Emperor Wen of Han there was no headcloth such as this; it is something made since Emperor Wen's time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers, but none could identify it. Ze answered: "I respectfully observe that before Emperor Wen of Han there was no such headcloth; it must have been made since Emperor Wen's reign.

sentences.zh: 臣見魏大司農盧元明撰《嵩高山廟記》雲，有神人，以玉為形，像長數寸，或出或隱，出則令世延長。

translations.literal: I have seen in the Record of the Songshan Shrine by Lu Yuanming, Grand Minister of Agriculture of Wei, that there was a divine person in jade form, the image several inches long, appearing and vanishing; when it appeared, the age was prolonged.
translations.idiomatic: I have read in Lu Yuanming's Record of the Songshan Shrine, written when he was Grand Minister of Agriculture of Wei, that a divine being took form in jade only a few inches long, appearing and disappearing; when it appeared, the age was lengthened.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下應天順民，定鼎嵩洛，嶽神自見，臣敢稱慶。」

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty responds to Heaven and follows the people, establishing the tripod at Song and Luo—the mountain god has appeared of itself; I dare proclaim congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty responds to Heaven and accords with the people, establishing the capital at Song and Luo; the mountain god has revealed himself— I dare offer congratulations."

sentences.zh: 因再拜，百官畢賀，天子大悅，賜縑二百匹。

translations.literal: He then bowed twice; all officials congratulated; the Son of Heaven was greatly pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice; all the officials congratulated him; the emperor was greatly pleased and granted him two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 從駕登太行山，詔問賾曰：「何處有羊腸阪？」

translations.literal: Accompanying the imperial procession up Mount Taihang, an edict asked Ze: "Where is Yangchang Slope?"
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying the emperor up Mount Taihang, he was asked by imperial edict: "Where is Yangchang Slope?"

sentences.zh: 賾對曰：「臣按《漢書·地理志》，上党壺關縣有羊腸阪。」

translations.literal: Ze replied: "According to the Geography Monograph of the Book of Han, Huchang County in Shangdang has Yangchang Slope."
translations.idiomatic: Ze answered: "According to the Geography Monograph in the Book of Han, Yangchang Slope is in Huchang County, Shangdang."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「不是。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "That is not it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is not the one."

sentences.zh: 又答曰：「臣按皇甫士安撰《地書》雲，太原北九十裡有羊腸阪。」

translations.literal: He answered again: "According to the Geographic Book by Huangfu Mi, ninety li north of Taiyuan there is Yangchang Slope."
translations.idiomatic: He answered again: "According to Huangfu Mi's Geographic Book, Yangchang Slope lies ninety li north of Taiyuan."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「是也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "That is it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is the one."

sentences.zh: 因謂牛弘曰：「崔祖浚所謂問一知二。」

translations.literal: He then said to Niu Hong: "That is what Cui Zujun means by 'ask one and know two.'"
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Niu Hong: "This is what Cui Zujun meant by 'ask one and know two.'"

sentences.zh: 五年，受詔與諸儒撰《區宇圖志》二百五十卷，奏之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he received an edict to compile with various scholars the Geographic Records in 250 volumes, and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was ordered to compile, with other scholars, the Geographic Records in 250 volumes, and submitted the work.

sentences.zh: 帝不善之，更令虞世基、許善心衍為六百卷。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased with it and had Yu Shiji and Xu Shanxin expand it to six hundred volumes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was dissatisfied with it and had Yu Shiji and Xu Shanxin expand it to six hundred volumes.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職，尋起令視事。

translations.literal: On his father's death he left office; soon he was restored and ordered to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he resigned, but was soon recalled and ordered back to duty.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，授鷹揚長史，置遼東郡縣名，皆賾之議也。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was appointed Chief Secretary of the Eagle-Flying Guard; the names of the Liaodong commanderies and counties established were all Ze's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he was made Chief Secretary of the Eagle-Flying Guard; the names chosen for the new Liaodong commanderies and counties were all proposed by Ze.

sentences.zh: 奉詔作《東征記》。

translations.literal: By imperial order he wrote the Record of the Eastern Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he composed the Record of the Eastern Expedition.

sentences.zh: 九年，除越王長史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Chief Secretary to the Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Chief Secretary to the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 于時山東盜賊蜂起，帝令撫慰高陽、襄國，歸首者八百餘人。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in swarms east of the mountains; the Emperor ordered him to pacify Gaoyang and Xiangguo; more than eight hundred surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits were rising throughout the east; the emperor sent him to pacify Gaoyang and Xiangguo, and more than eight hundred men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從駕江都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he accompanied the imperial procession to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之弑帝也，引為著作郎，稱疾不起。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji assassinated the Emperor, Ze was appointed Compiler but pleaded illness and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, Ze was offered the post of Compiler but pleaded illness and refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 在路發疾，卒于彭城，時年六十九。

translations.literal: On the road he fell ill and died at Pengcheng, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the road and died at Pengcheng at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 賾與洛陽元善、河東柳抃、太原王劭、吳興姚察、琅邪諸葛潁、信都劉焯、河間劉炫相善，每因休假，清談竟日。

translations.literal: Ze was on good terms with Yuan Shan of Luoyang, Liu Bian of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langya, Liu Chuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; whenever they had a holiday they would hold pure conversation all day.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was close friends with Yuan Shan of Luoyang, Liu Bian of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langya, Liu Chuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; on holidays they would talk together from morning till night.

sentences.zh: 所著詞賦碑誌十余萬言，撰《洽聞志》七卷，《八代四科志》三十卷，未及施行，江都傾覆，鹹為煨燼。

translations.literal: He wrote more than a hundred thousand characters in rhapsodies, inscriptions, and epitaphs; compiled the Comprehensive Records of Notable Knowledge in seven volumes and the Records of the Four Categories across Eight Dynasties in thirty volumes; before they could be implemented, Jiangdu was overthrown and all were consumed by fire.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than a hundred thousand characters of verse, inscriptions, and epitaphs, and compiled the Comprehensive Records of Notable Knowledge in seven volumes and the Records of the Four Categories across Eight Dynasties in thirty volumes; before these could be put into use, Jiangdu fell and all were burned to ash.

sentences.zh: ○徐則

translations.literal: ○ Xu Ze
translations.idiomatic: ○ Xu Ze

sentences.zh: 徐則，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Xu Ze was a native of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ze was a native of Tan in Donghai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼沈靜，寡嗜欲。

translations.literal: From youth he was quiet and still, with few desires.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was calm and reserved, with little appetite for worldly things.

sentences.zh: 受業于周弘正，善三玄，精於議論，聲擅都邑，則歎曰：「名者實之賓，吾其為賓乎！」

translations.literal: He studied under Zhou Hongzheng, was skilled in the Three Mysterious Learning, excelled in disputation, and his fame dominated the capital; Ze sighed and said: "Fame is the guest of reality—am I to be the guest?"
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Zhou Hongzheng, mastered the Three Mysterious Learning, and excelled in debate until his reputation filled the capital; Ze sighed and said: "Fame is the guest of substance—am I to be the guest?"

sentences.zh: 遂懷棲隱之操，杖策入縉雲山。

translations.literal: Thereupon he harbored the resolve to live in seclusion, took staff in hand, and entered Mount Jinyun.
translations.idiomatic: With that he resolved to live in seclusion, took up his staff, and withdrew to Mount Jinyun.

sentences.zh: 後學數百人，苦請教授，則謝而遣之。

translations.literal: Later several hundred students earnestly begged to be taught; Ze declined and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Later several hundred students pleaded to become his disciples, but Ze refused and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 不娶妻，常服巾褐。

translations.literal: He did not marry and regularly wore cloth cap and hemp robe.
translations.idiomatic: He never married and always wore a plain cap and hemp robe.

sentences.zh: 陳太建時，應召來憩於至真觀。

translations.literal: During the Taijian era of Chen, summoned, he came to rest at the Zhizhen Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taijian period of Chen he answered a summons and stayed for a time at the Zhizhen Abbey.

sentences.zh: 期月，又辭入天臺山，因絕穀養性，所資唯松水而已，雖隆冬洹寒，不服綿絮。

translations.literal: After a month he declined again and entered Mount Tiantai; there he ceased eating grain to nurture his nature, relying only on pine and water; even in the depths of winter's icy cold, he wore no cotton padding.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he declined further service and withdrew to Mount Tiantai, where he abstained from grain to nourish his nature and lived on pine and water alone; even in the bitter cold of midwinter he wore no padded clothes.

sentences.zh: 太傅徐陵為之刊山立頌。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Xu Ling carved a mountain inscription and erected a eulogy for him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Xu Ling had an inscription carved on the mountain and a eulogy erected in his honor.

sentences.zh: 初在縉雲山，太極真人徐君降之曰：「汝年出八十，當為王者師，然後得道也。」

translations.literal: When he was first on Mount Jinyun, the Perfected Man of the Grand Ultimate, Lord Xu, descended to him and said: "When your years pass eighty, you shall become teacher to a king—only then will you attain the Way."
translations.idiomatic: While he was still on Mount Jinyun, the Perfected Man of the Grand Ultimate, Lord Xu, appeared to him and said: "When you pass eighty, you will become a king's teacher, and only then will you attain the Way."

sentences.zh: 晉王廣鎮揚州，知其名，手書召之曰：「夫道得眾妙，法體自然，包涵二儀，混成萬物，人能弘道，道不虛行。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Guang garrisoned Yangzhou, learned his name, and wrote him a personal summons, saying: "The Way attains the myriad subtleties; the Law embodies nature; it embraces the two principles and blends to form the ten thousand things; if a man can expand the Way, the Way will not act in vain.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guang of Jin was stationed at Yangzhou, he learned Xu Ze's name and wrote him a personal summons: "The Way gathers all subtleties; the Law accords with nature; it embraces yin and yang and blends them into the ten thousand things. When a man can enlarge the Way, the Way does not pass in vain.

sentences.zh: 先生履德養空，宗玄齊物，深明義味，曉達法門。

translations.literal: You, Master, tread virtue and nurture emptiness, take the Mysterious as your standard and equalize things; you deeply understand the flavor of righteousness and clearly penetrate the gates of the Law.
translations.idiomatic: You, Master, practice virtue and cultivate emptiness, take the Mysterious as your guide and treat all things as equal; you deeply grasp the meaning of righteousness and clearly understand the gates of the Law.

sentences.zh: 悅性沖玄，怡神虛白，餐松餌術，棲息煙霞。

translations.literal: Your nature delights in the subtle and mysterious; your spirit is serene in empty whiteness; you dine on pine and feed on arts; you dwell in mist and rosy clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Your nature delights in purity and mystery; your spirit rests in tranquil emptiness; you feed on pine and live by alchemical arts, dwelling among mist and colored clouds.

sentences.zh: 望赤城而待風雲，遊玉堂而駕龍鳳，雖複藏名台嶽，猶且騰實江淮，藉甚嘉猷，有勞寤寐。

translations.literal: Gazing toward Chicheng while awaiting wind and clouds, roaming the Jade Hall while driving dragon and phoenix—though you hide your name on mountain peaks, your substance still soars in the Jiang-Huai; your excellent counsel is widely praised; I have toiled waking and sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: You gaze toward Mount Chicheng awaiting wind and clouds, roam the Jade Hall borne by dragon and phoenix; though you hide your name on lofty peaks, your worth still shines across the Jiang-Huai, and your fine counsel has long occupied my thoughts day and night.

sentences.zh: 欽承素道，久積虛襟，側席幽人，夢想岩穴。

translations.literal: I reverently inherit the pure Way and have long stored an empty breast; I sit askance awaiting the recluse and dream of mountain caves.
translations.idiomatic: I reverently honor the pure Way and have long kept an open heart; I sit with seat askew awaiting a recluse and dream of life in mountain caves.

sentences.zh: 霜風已冷，海氣將寒，偃息茂林，道體休悆。

translations.literal: Frost wind has already turned cold and sea air will soon be chill; rest in the lush forest—your Way-body is at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The frost wind has turned cold and the sea air is growing chill; rest in the deep forest and let your body of the Way find its ease.

sentences.zh: 昔商山四皓，輕舉漢庭，淮南八公，來儀籓邸。

translations.literal: Formerly the Four Hoary Heads of Mount Shang lightly rose to the Han court; the Eight Lords of Huainan came in ritual to a prince's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Four Hoary Heads of Mount Shang readily entered the Han court, and the Eight Lords of Huainan came to serve at a prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 古今雖異，山谷不殊，市朝之隱，前賢已說，導凡述聖，非先生而誰！

translations.literal: Past and present differ, yet valleys and hills are not different; reclusion in the marketplace—former sages have already spoken of it; to guide the common and declare the sage—if not you, Master, then who!
translations.idiomatic: Times may change, but mountains and valleys remain the same; sages of old already spoke of hiding in plain sight within the city; to guide the ordinary and expound the sacred—if not you, Master, then who?

sentences.zh: 故遣使人，往彼延請，想無勞束帶，賁然來思，不待蒲輪，去彼空穀。

translations.literal: Therefore I send an envoy to go there and invite you; I think you need not trouble to gird your sash—come splendidly; wait not for the rush-wheeled carriage—leave that empty valley.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I send an envoy to invite you; I trust you need not trouble to dress formally—come at once in splendid readiness, without waiting for a carriage of rush wheels to draw you from your empty valley.

sentences.zh: 希能屈己，佇望披雲。」

translations.literal: I hope you can humble yourself; I stand awaiting the parting of clouds."
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will condescend to come; I stand waiting for the clouds to part."

sentences.zh: 則謂門人曰：「吾今年八十一，王來召我，徐君之旨，信而有徵。」

translations.literal: Ze told his disciples: "I am eighty-one this year; the Prince has come to summon me—the words of Lord Xu are trustworthy and have proof."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ze told his disciples: "I am eighty-one this year, and the Prince has summoned me; Lord Xu's prophecy has proved true."

sentences.zh: 於是遂詣揚州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With that he set out for Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉王將請受道法，則辭以時日不便。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin was about to request instruction in the Way and its methods, Ze declined on the grounds that the time was not suitable.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin was about to receive instruction in the Way, Ze declined, saying the time was not auspicious.

sentences.zh: 其後夕中，命侍者取香火，如平常朝禮之儀。

translations.literal: That evening he ordered his attendants to fetch incense and fire and performed the usual rites of morning audience.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he had his attendants bring incense and performed the rites he usually observed at dawn.

sentences.zh: 至於五更而死，支體柔弱如生，停留數旬，顏色無變。

translations.literal: At the fifth watch he died; his limbs were soft as in life; for several tens of days his complexion did not change.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth watch he died; his body remained supple as in life, and for several weeks his complexion did not change.

sentences.zh: 晉王下書曰：「天臺真隱東海徐先生，虛確居宗，沖玄成德，齊物處外，檢行安身。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin issued a document: "The true recluse of Tiantai, Master Xu of Donghai—empty certainty as his standard, subtle mystery as his completed virtue, equalizing things while dwelling outside, restraining conduct to settle his person.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin issued a proclamation: "The true recluse of Tiantai, Master Xu of Donghai, took emptiness and certainty as his foundation, subtle mystery as his completed virtue, treated all things as equal while dwelling apart from the world, and disciplined his conduct to preserve his person.

sentences.zh: 草褐蒲衣，餐松餌術，棲隱靈岳，五十餘年。

translations.literal: In grass cloak and rush garment, dining on pine and feeding on arts, dwelling hidden on spirit peaks—for more than fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: Clad in grass and rush, feeding on pine and living by alchemical arts, he dwelt hidden on sacred mountains for more than fifty years.

sentences.zh: 卓矣仙才，飄然勝氣，千尋萬頃，莫測其涯。

translations.literal: Transcendent talent surpassing others, an ethereal victor's spirit—a thousand fathoms, ten thousand acres, none can measure its bounds.
translations.idiomatic: His transcendent gifts were extraordinary, his spirit lofty and free; like a thousand fathoms of depth or ten thousand acres of breadth, none could fathom his limits.

sentences.zh: 寡人欽承道風，久餐德素，頻遣使乎，遠此延屈，冀得虔受上法，式建良緣。

translations.literal: I have reverently inherited the wind of the Way and long fed on pure virtue; repeatedly I sent envoys to invite you from afar, hoping devoutly to receive the supreme Law and firmly establish a good bond.
translations.idiomatic: I have long reverenced the wind of the Way and nourished myself on your pure virtue; again and again I sent envoys to invite you from afar, hoping devoutly to receive the supreme teaching and establish a worthy bond.

sentences.zh: 至此甫爾，未淹旬日，厭塵羽化，反真靈府。

translations.literal: He had only just arrived, not ten days full, when he wearied of the dust, transformed in feather, and returned to the true numinous realm.
translations.idiomatic: He had only just arrived, less than ten days ago, when he cast off the dusty world, ascended in transformation, and returned to the true realm of spirit.

sentences.zh: 身體柔軟，顏色不變，經方所謂屍解地仙者哉！

translations.literal: His body soft and supple, his color unchanged—is this not what medical classics call corpse liberation into an earthly immortal!
translations.idiomatic: His body remained soft and his complexion unchanged—is this not what the medical classics call corpse liberation and earthly immortality!

sentences.zh: 誠複師禮未申，而心許有在，雖忘怛化，猶愴於懷，喪事所資，隨須供給。

translations.literal: Truly teacher's rites were not yet fulfilled, yet a promise of the heart remains; though I forget sorrow at his transformation, grief still lodges in my breast; whatever the funeral requires, supply it as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Though the rites of discipleship were never completed, my heart had already pledged itself to him; though I should rejoice in his transformation, sorrow still fills my breast; provide whatever his funeral requires.

sentences.zh: 霓裳羽蓋，既且騰雲，空槨餘衣，詎藉墳壟！

translations.literal: Rainbow robes and feathered canopies—already he mounts the clouds; an empty coffin and leftover garments—how could he rely on mound and tomb!
translations.idiomatic: Rainbow robes and feathered canopies—he has already ascended on clouds; an empty coffin and leftover garments—what need has he of mound and tomb!

sentences.zh: 但杖為猶存，示同俗法，宜遣使人，送還天臺定葬。」

translations.literal: Only his staff remains, to show conformity with common custom; you should send envoys to return him to Tiantai for proper burial."
translations.idiomatic: Only his staff remains, to show conformity with ordinary custom; send envoys to return him to Mount Tiantai for proper burial."

sentences.zh: 是時自江都至於天臺，在道多見則徒步，雲得放還。

translations.literal: At that time from Jiangdu to Tiantai, on the road many saw Ze walking on foot, saying he had been released to return.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, from Jiangdu to Mount Tiantai, travelers on the road often saw Ze walking on foot, saying he had been released to return.

sentences.zh: 至其舊居，取經書道法，分遺弟子，仍令淨掃一房，曰：「若有客至，宜延之於此。」

translations.literal: When he reached his old dwelling, he took scriptures and Daoist methods and distributed them among his disciples; he also had a room swept clean and said, "If guests come, you should receive them here."
translations.idiomatic: When he reached his old dwelling, he took his scriptures and Daoist texts and distributed them among his disciples; he had a room swept clean and said, "If guests come, receive them here."

sentences.zh: 然後跨石樑而去，不知所之。

translations.literal: Then he crossed a stone bridge and departed—none knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: Then he crossed a stone bridge and departed—to where, no one knew.

sentences.zh: 須臾，屍柩至，方知其靈化。

translations.literal: In a moment the coffin with his corpse arrived, and only then did they know of his spiritual transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the coffin with his body arrived, and only then did they understand that he had undergone spiritual transformation.

sentences.zh: 時年八十二。

translations.literal: He was then eighty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty-two years old at the time.

sentences.zh: 晉王聞而益異之，賵物千段，遣畫工圖其狀貌，令柳抃為之贊曰：「可道非道，常道無名。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin heard and was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand lengths of goods as funeral gifts, had painters depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Bian to compose an encomium, saying, "The Way that can be spoken is not the eternal Way; the eternal Way has no name.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin heard this and was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand lengths of goods as funeral gifts, had painters depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Bian to compose an encomium that began, "The Way that can be spoken is not the eternal Way; the eternal Way has no name.

sentences.zh: 上德不德，至德無盈。

translations.literal: The highest virtue is not virtuous; the utmost virtue has no fullness.
translations.idiomatic: The highest virtue is not virtuous; the utmost virtue has no fullness.

sentences.zh: 玄風扇矣，而有先生。

translations.literal: The mysterious wind has fanned forth, and there was the Master.
translations.idiomatic: The mysterious wind had spread abroad, and there was the Master.

sentences.zh: 夙煉金液，怡神玉清。

translations.literal: Long he refined golden elixir, delighting his spirit in jade purity.
translations.idiomatic: Long he refined the golden elixir, delighting his spirit in jade purity.

sentences.zh: 石髓方軟，雲丹欲成。

translations.literal: Stone marrow had just softened; cloud cinnabar was about to be perfected.
translations.idiomatic: Stone marrow had just softened; cloud cinnabar was about to be perfected.

sentences.zh: 言追葛稚，將侶茅嬴。

translations.literal: He spoke of following Ge Hong and would take as companion Mao Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of following Ge Hong and would take Mao Ying as his companion.

sentences.zh: 我王遙屬，爰感靈誠。

translations.literal: Our prince from afar was attached to him and thus felt his numinous sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Our prince from afar was drawn to him and thus felt his numinous sincerity.

sentences.zh: 柱下暫啟，河上沉精。

translations.literal: For a time he opened the pillar beneath; on the river he sank his essence.
translations.idiomatic: For a time he opened the pillar beneath; on the river he sank his essence.

sentences.zh: 留符告信，化杖飛聲。

translations.literal: He left a talisman to announce faith; transforming his staff, he flew with a sound.
translations.idiomatic: He left a talisman to announce his faith; transforming his staff, he flew away with a sound.

sentences.zh: 永思靈跡，曷用攄情？

translations.literal: Forever thinking on his numinous traces—how may one give vent to feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Forever thinking on his numinous traces—how may one give full vent to feeling?

sentences.zh: 時披素繪，如臨赤城。」

translations.literal: At times one spreads the plain painting, as if facing Red Wall."
translations.idiomatic: At times one spreads the plain portrait, as if facing Red Wall."

sentences.zh: 時有建安宋玉泉、會稽孔道茂、丹陽王遠知等，亦行辟穀，以松水自給，皆為煬帝所重。

translations.literal: At the time there were Song Yuquan of Jian'an, Kong Daomao of Kuaiji, Wang Yuanzhi of Danyang, and others who also practiced grain avoidance, sustaining themselves on pine water—all were valued by Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were Song Yuquan of Jian'an, Kong Daomao of Kuaiji, Wang Yuanzhi of Danyang, and others who also practiced grain avoidance and sustained themselves on pine water—all were valued by Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: ○張文詡

translations.literal: ○ Zhang Wenxu
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhang Wenxu

sentences.zh: 張文詡，河東人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenxu was a native of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenxu was a native of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父琚，開皇中為洹水令，以清正聞。

translations.literal: His father Ju, in the Kaihuang era served as Magistrate of Huanshui and was known for purity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ju served as Magistrate of Huanshui during the Kaihuang era and was known for purity and uprightness.

sentences.zh: 有書數千卷，教訓子侄，皆以明經自達。

translations.literal: He had several thousand volumes of books and instructed his sons and nephews, all of whom attained office through mastery of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He owned several thousand volumes of books and instructed his sons and nephews, all of whom attained office through mastery of the classics.

sentences.zh: 文詡博覽文籍，特精《三禮》，其《周易》、《詩》、《書》及《春秋三傳》，並皆通習。

translations.literal: Wenxu read broadly in literary works and was especially expert in the Three Rites; the Changes, Odes, Documents, and the three commentaries to the Spring and Autumn—all he mastered thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxu read broadly in literary works and was especially expert in the Three Rites; the Book of Changes, Book of Odes, Book of Documents, and the three commentaries to the Spring and Autumn Annals—all he mastered thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 每好鄭玄注解，以為通博，其諸儒異說，亦皆詳究焉。

translations.literal: He always favored Zheng Xuan's commentaries, considering them comprehensive and broad; the varying doctrines of other Ru scholars he also investigated in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He always favored Zheng Xuan's commentaries, considering them comprehensive and penetrating; the varying doctrines of other scholars he also investigated in detail.

sentences.zh: 高祖引致天下名儒碩學之士，其房暉遠、張仲讓、孔籠之徒，並延之于博士之位。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu drew in famous Ru scholars and eminent learned men from all the empire; Fang Xianyuan, Zhang Zhongrang, Kong Long, and their kind were all extended invitations to the post of Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu drew in famous scholars and eminent learned men from across the empire; Fang Xianyuan, Zhang Zhongrang, Kong Long, and their kind were all invited to serve as Erudites.

sentences.zh: 文詡時遊太學，暉遠等莫不推伏之，學內翕然，咸共宗仰。

translations.literal: When Wenxu visited the Imperial Academy, Xianyuan and the others all deferred to him; within the academy there was harmony, and all together revered him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxu visited the Imperial Academy, Xianyuan and the others all deferred to him; within the academy there was harmony, and all revered him together.

sentences.zh: 其門生多詣文詡，請質凝滯，文詡輒博引證據，辨說無窮，唯其所擇。

translations.literal: His students often went to Wenxu to request clarification of points that troubled them; Wenxu would broadly cite evidence and argue without end, following only what he chose.
translations.idiomatic: His students often went to Wenxu to request clarification of points that troubled them; Wenxu would cite evidence broadly and argue without end, following only the course he chose.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史皇甫誕一時朝彥，恆執弟子之禮。

translations.literal: Huangfu Dan, Attending Secretary in the Imperial Library, was a leading figure of the court in his day and always observed the rites of a disciple toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Dan, Attending Secretary in the Imperial Library, was a leading figure of the court in his day and always observed the rites of a disciple toward him.

sentences.zh: 適至南台，遽飾所乘馬，就學邀屈。

translations.literal: When he happened to reach the Southern Terrace, he hastily adorned the horse he rode and went to the academy to invite and detain Wenxu.
translations.idiomatic: When he happened to reach the Southern Terrace, he hastily adorned the horse he rode and went to the academy to invite Wenxu to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 文詡每牽馬步進，意在不因人以自致也。

translations.literal: Wenxu always led the horse and walked alongside, his intent being not to advance himself by relying on others.
