translations.idiomatic: Wenxu always led the horse and walked alongside, his intent being not to advance himself by relying on others.

sentences.zh: 右僕射蘇威聞其名而召之，與語，大悅，勸令從官。

translations.literal: Su Wei, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, heard his name and summoned him; after conversing with him he was greatly pleased and urged him to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, heard his name and summoned him; after conversing with him he was greatly pleased and urged him to take office.

sentences.zh: 文詡意不在仕，固辭焉。

translations.literal: Wenxu's intent was not in office; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxu had no wish to serve in office and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，學廢，文詡策杖而歸，灌園為業。

translations.literal: At the end of the Renshou era the academy was abolished; Wenxu leaned on his staff and returned home, making irrigation and gardening his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Renshou era the academy was abolished; Wenxu leaned on his staff and returned home, making irrigation and gardening his occupation.

sentences.zh: 州郡頻舉，皆不應命。

translations.literal: The province and commandery repeatedly recommended him, but he never responded to summons.
translations.idiomatic: The province and commandery repeatedly recommended him, but he never responded to summons.

sentences.zh: 事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He became known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He became known for his filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 每以德化人，鄉黨頗移風俗。

translations.literal: He always transformed people through virtue, and the village and district considerably shifted their customs.
translations.idiomatic: He always transformed people through virtue, and the village and district considerably shifted their customs.

sentences.zh: 嘗有人夜中竊刈其麥者，見而避之，盜因感悟，棄麥而謝。

translations.literal: Once someone stole and reaped his wheat at night; Wenxu saw him and withdrew, and the thief, moved by this, abandoned the wheat and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Once someone stole and reaped his wheat at night; Wenxu saw him and withdrew, and the thief, moved by this, abandoned the wheat and apologized.

sentences.zh: 文詡慰諭之，自誓不言，固令持去。

translations.literal: Wenxu comforted and instructed him, swore himself not to speak of it, and firmly had him take the wheat away.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxu comforted him, swore himself not to speak of it, and firmly had him take the wheat away.

sentences.zh: 經數年，盜者向鄉人說之，始為遠近所悉。

translations.literal: After several years the thief told fellow townspeople of it, and only then was it known far and near.
translations.idiomatic: After several years the thief told fellow townspeople of it, and only then was it known far and near.

sentences.zh: 鄰家築牆，心有不直，文詡因毀舊堵以應之。

translations.literal: A neighbor built a wall with a mind not quite straight; Wenxu therefore tore down his old wall to match it.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor built a wall that was not quite straight; Wenxu therefore tore down his old wall to match it.

sentences.zh: 文詡嘗有腰疾，會醫者自言善禁，文詡令禁之，遂為刃所傷，至於頓伏床枕。

translations.literal: Wenxu once had a pain in his lower back; it happened that a physician claimed skill in spell-binding; Wenxu had him perform it and was wounded by a blade, to the point of collapsing on bed and pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxu once had a pain in his lower back; a physician who claimed skill in spell-binding treated him and wounded him with a blade, so that he collapsed on his bed.

sentences.zh: 醫者叩頭請罪，文詡遽遣之，因為其隱，謂妻子曰：「吾昨風眩，落坑所致。」

translations.literal: The physician kowtowed and begged forgiveness; Wenxu immediately sent him away and covered the matter for him, telling his wife and children, "Yesterday I had a dizzy spell from wind and fell into a pit—that is what caused it."
translations.idiomatic: The physician kowtowed and begged forgiveness; Wenxu immediately sent him away and covered the matter for him, telling his wife and children, "Yesterday I had a dizzy spell and fell into a pit—that is what caused it."

sentences.zh: 其掩人之短，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His covering of others' faults was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His way of covering others' faults was all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 州縣以其貧素，將加振恤，輒辭不受。

translations.literal: The province and county, because he was poor and plain, were about to add relief and support, but he always declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The province and county, because he was poor and plain, were about to offer relief and support, but he always declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 每閒居無事，從容長歎曰：「老冉冉而將至，恐修名之不立！」

translations.literal: Whenever at leisure with nothing to do, he would calmly sigh long and say, "Old age comes on gradually—I fear a cultivated name will not be established!"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever at leisure with nothing to do, he would calmly sigh and say, "Old age comes on gradually—I fear a cultivated name will not be established!"

sentences.zh: 以如意擊幾，皆有處所，時人方之閔子騫原憲焉。

translations.literal: He would strike the armrest with his ruyi scepter, each blow landing in its place; men of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He would strike the armrest with his ruyi scepter, each blow landing in its place; men of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.

sentences.zh: 終於家，年四十。

translations.literal: He died at home, aged forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 鄉人為立碑頌，號曰張先生。

translations.literal: Fellow townspeople erected a stele in praise of him and called him Master Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townspeople erected a stele in praise of him and called him Master Zhang.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古之所謂隱逸者，非伏其身而不見也，非閉其言而不出也，非藏其智而不發也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: What the ancients called recluses was not hiding the body so it would not be seen, not closing the words so they would not come forth, not concealing wisdom so it would not be released.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: What the ancients called recluses was not hiding the body so it would not be seen, not closing the words so they would not come forth, not concealing wisdom so it would not be released.

sentences.zh: 蓋以恬淡為心，不曒不昧，安時處順，與物無私者也。

translations.literal: Rather, with tranquil indifference as their heart, neither bright nor dim, they rested in the times and accorded with circumstance, without selfishness toward things.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, with tranquil indifference as their heart, neither bright nor dim, they rested in the times and accorded with circumstance, without selfishness toward things.

sentences.zh: 士謙等忘懷纓冕，畢志丘園，隱不違親，貞不絕俗，不教而勸，虛往實歸，愛之如父母，懷之如親戚，非有自然之純德，其孰能至於斯乎？

translations.literal: Shiqian and the others forgot official caps and robes, fulfilled their resolve in field and garden, hid without violating kinship, were chaste without cutting off the vulgar, urged without teaching, went forth empty and returned full; people loved them as parents and cherished them as kin—without natural pure virtue, who could reach this?
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian and the others forgot official caps and robes, fulfilled their resolve in field and garden, lived in reclusion without violating kinship, were steadfast without cutting themselves off from the world, urged without teaching, went forth empty and returned full; people loved them as parents and cherished them as kin—without natural pure virtue, who could reach this?

sentences.zh: 然士謙聞譽不喜，文詡見傷無慍，徐則志在沉冥，不可親疏，莫能貴賤，皆抱樸之士矣。

translations.literal: Yet Shiqian, hearing praise, was not pleased; Wenxu, seeing injury, was not angry; Ze's aim lay in deep obscurity—none could draw him near or push him away, none could make him noble or base—all were men who embraced simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shiqian, hearing praise, was not pleased; Wenxu, seeing injury, was not angry; Ze's aim lay in deep obscurity—none could draw him near or push him away, none could make him noble or base—all were men who embraced simplicity.

sentences.zh: 崔廓感於屈辱，遂以肥遁見稱，祖浚文籍之美，足以克隆先構，父子雖動靜殊方，其于成名一也，美哉！

translations.literal: Cui Kuo, stirred by humiliation, came to be praised for his ample withdrawal; Zujun's literary beauty was sufficient to continue and enlarge the ancestral structure—father and son, though active and still in different directions, in achieving fame were one; how fine!
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuo, stirred by humiliation, came to be praised for his ample withdrawal; Zujun's literary brilliance was sufficient to continue and enlarge the ancestral achievement—father and son, though active and still in different directions, in achieving fame were one; how fine!
